title: In vivo chromatin immunoprecipitation protocol for mouse liver nuclei
author: Li, Akl, et al.
materials: CFX384 Touch Real-Time PCR Detection System

An aliquot of sheared chromatin is reverse-crosslinked and purified using PCR purification kit. The size range of chromatin is analyzed by electrophoresis. DNA concentration is measured by NanoDrop.8.Thaw aliquoted chromatin from step 7, which contains 50 μL sheared chromatin and add 150 μL 1× ChIP elution buffer.9.Add 8 μL 5 M NaCl to each sample, mix and then incubate at 95°C for 15 min. Afterward, cool samples to room temperature.10.Purify and collect DNA in 50 μL of elution buffer. This protocol used the GeneJET PCR Purification Kit from Thermo Fisher (https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2FMAN0012662_GeneJET_PCR_Purification_UG.pdf).11.Use 10 μL sample and determine DNA fragment size by electrophoresis on a 1.5% agarose gel with a 100 base pair DNA marker (Troubleshooting 2).12.To determine DNA concentration, transfer 2 μL of purified DNA to NanoDrop. The concentration of DNA should be 50–90 ng/μL.

steps.title: Isolate DNA‑protein complexes
steps.instruction: Lyse cross‑linked liver nuclei with DNAzol, precipitate DNA‑protein complexes, wash, denature, and resuspend in IP buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL DNAzol reagent to the nuclei pellet (or 1 mL per 100 mg homogenized tissue) and resuspend with a wide‑bore tip (cut 2–3 mm from tip).
Incubate 15 min at room temperature with gentle rotation; do NOT centrifuge after this step.
Add 2.5 mL ice‑cold 100 % ethanol (half the volume of DNAzol used) and mix by inversion.
Incubate at –20 °C for 1 h to precipitate DNA‑protein complexes.
Prepare protein denature buffer during the precipitation step.
Centrifuge at 4000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 5 mL ice‑cold 75 % ethanol (same volume as DNAzol used).
Centrifuge again at 4000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Air‑dry pellet for 5–15 s.
Add 5 mL protein denature buffer (or same volume as DNAzol used) and incubate 30 min at 37 °C with gentle shaking to remove non‑covalently bound proteins.
Add 5 mL 5 M NaCl (equal volume to protein denature buffer) and incubate 30 min at 37 °C.
Add 1 mL (0.1 × volume) 3 M sodium acetate and 30 mL (3 × volume) ice‑cold 100 % ethanol.
Incubate at –20 °C for 1 h to precipitate purified DNA and DNA‑protein complexes.
Centrifuge at 4000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet and wash with 25 mL ice‑cold 75 % ethanol.
Centrifuge at 4000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant and keep on ice.
Repeat the resuspend‑wash‑centrifuge cycle two more times for a total of three washes.
Air‑dry pellet for 10 min at room temperature.
Dissolve pellet on ice with 5 mL IP buffer containing 0.5 % SDS and protease inhibitor cocktail (add 250 µL 10 % SDS and 100 µL 50× protease inhibitor to 4750 µL IP buffer).
Optional: Save 50 µL aliquot as a pre‑sonication control; an additional aliquot can be saved for western‑blot verification.

steps.title: Assess sheared chromatin quality
steps.instruction: Reverse‑crosslink an aliquot of sheared chromatin, purify DNA, and evaluate fragment size and concentration.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the 50 µL sheared chromatin (from step r) and add 150 µL 1× ChIP elution buffer.
Add 8 µL 5 M NaCl, mix, then incubate at 95 °C for 15 min; cool to room temperature.
Purify DNA using the GeneJET PCR Purification Kit and elute in 50 µL elution buffer.
Run 10 µL of purified DNA on a 1.5 % agarose gel with a 100 bp DNA marker to assess fragment size.
Transfer 2 µL of purified DNA to a NanoDrop; expected concentration 50–90 ng/µL.

steps.title: Purify ChIP DNA and perform qPCR
steps.instruction: Reverse‑crosslink ChIP samples, purify DNA, dilute, and run SYBR‑Green qPCR to quantify enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge ChIP eluates at 10,000 g for 10 s to collect condensed sample from the cap.
Purify DNA with the same PCR purification kit as above, eluting in 50 µL elution buffer (follow manufacturer’s instructions).
Pause point: Eluted DNA can be stored at 20°C or used immediately for qPCR.
Dilute eluted DNA 1:2 with nuclease‑free water; use 2 µL of the diluted DNA per qPCR reaction.
Prepare qPCR master mix per 15 µL reaction: 2 µL diluted DNA template, 7.5 µL 2× SYBR mix, 1 µL forward primer (10 µM), 1 µL reverse primer (10 µM), 3.5 µL ddH₂O.
Include appropriate positive and negative control primers.

Run qPCR with the following cycling conditions: 50 °C 2 min (UDG pre‑treatment), 95 °C 2 min initial denaturation, then 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s denaturation, 60 °C 15 s annealing, 72 °C 1 min extension; final extension 72 °C 10 min, hold at 4 °C.
